note: All organizations, people, and domains are fictional. Only reserved .example and .test domains are used (RFC 2606).

scenarios.label: phishing
scenarios.context: The week after midterms, this email arrives in your student inbox.

email.subject: Your midterm grade has been updated
body: Hello,
Your instructor has published an updated midterm grade for one of your courses. Please review it before the grade-appeal window closes on Friday.
View your grade here:

feedback.explanation: This is phishing. The visible link text shows the real NorthLearn address, but the link really goes to grade-portal.test. The words northbridge.example are only a label placed in front of someone else's domain. Sender addresses can be forged, so the real link destination is the deciding cue.
cues: The link text and the real destination do not match
Read the domain from right to left: it is grade-portal.test
Mild time pressure about an appeal deadline
feedback.safe_action: Do not click. Open NorthLearn from your bookmark or by typing the address yourself, then report the message to IT Services.

scenarios.label: legitimate
scenarios.context: The university's IT department sends this notice to all students.

email.subject: Planned maintenance this Saturday, 02:00 to 04:00
body: Dear students and staff,
NorthLearn and the student portal will be unavailable this Saturday from 02:00 to 04:00 while we install security updates. No action is required from you.
Reminder: IT Services will never ask for your password by email, phone, or chat.
IT Services, Northbridge University

feedback.explanation: This is legitimate. It comes from the official northbridge.example domain, asks you to do nothing, contains no link or attachment, and even reminds you that IT never asks for passwords.
cues: The sender's domain exactly matches the university domain
Information only: no request for passwords, payments, or personal details
No link or attachment to open
feedback.safe_action: No action is needed. If in doubt, check the IT status page by typing its address yourself.

scenarios.label: phishing
scenarios.context: This email lands in your inbox late on a Friday afternoon.

email.subject: FINAL NOTICE: Enrollment cancellation at 5:00 PM today
body: Dear Student,
Our records show an unpaid balance on your account. If payment is not received by 5:00 PM TODAY, your enrollment will be cancelled and you will lose access to all courses.
Pay immediately to avoid cancellation:

feedback.explanation: This is phishing. An extreme same-day deadline and the threat of losing your enrollment are designed to rush you. Real finance offices give notice well in advance and point you to the official portal. The sender's domain, northbridge-payments.example, is also not the university's domain.
cues: Artificial same-day deadline
Threat of a severe consequence
Payment link on a look-alike domain
feedback.safe_action: Pause. Check your balance by signing in to the student portal you normally use, or contact the Finance Office using details from the official website.

scenarios.label: phishing
scenarios.context: You tapped a link in a text message saying your timetable had changed. This page opened.

web.heading: Student Portal sign in
body: Your timetable has changed. Sign in to see the update.

feedback.explanation: This is phishing. The page copies the real portal's look, and the padlock shows the connection is encrypted, but a padlock protects the connection, not the identity of the site. The domain is northbridge-portal-login.test, not northbridge.example.
cues: The domain is not the university's domain
A padlock does not prove a site is genuine
You arrived through an unexpected text-message link
feedback.safe_action: Close the page. Open the portal yourself by typing portal.northbridge.example or using your bookmark.

scenarios.label: legitimate
scenarios.context: You reserved a library book last week.

email.subject: Your reserved book is ready for pickup
body: Hello,
The book you reserved, Introduction to Network Security, is ready at the circulation desk on the ground floor. It will be held for seven days.
Please bring your student card when you collect it.
Northbridge Library

feedback.explanation: This is legitimate. The sender's domain is exactly northbridge.example, the message matches something you actually did, and it asks you to act in person rather than click a link or sign in.
cues: Exact official domain after the @ sign
An expected message linked to your own action
No link, attachment, or request for information
feedback.safe_action: Collect the book as described.

scenarios.label: legitimate
scenarios.context: In class yesterday, your instructor said she would email the lab worksheet.

email.subject: Week 5 lab worksheet (as discussed in class)
body: Hi all,
As promised in yesterday's session, the Week 5 lab worksheet is attached. It is also posted on NorthLearn under Week 5.
Best regards,
Prof. Rahman

feedback.explanation: This is legitimate. The attachment was announced in class, it comes from your instructor's official address, it is an ordinary PDF, and the same file is available on NorthLearn.
cues: The attachment was expected and announced in advance
Official instructor address
The same file is available through the LMS
feedback.safe_action: It is reasonable to open it, or download the same file from NorthLearn if you prefer.

scenarios.label: phishing
scenarios.context: This message arrives while you are studying for exams.

email.subject: Mailbox storage limit reached
body: Dear Student,
Your mailbox has reached 99% of its storage limit. New messages, including course announcements, may be rejected.
Use the link below to increase your storage free of charge:

feedback.explanation: This is phishing. Look closely at the sender: northbrldge.example replaces the letter i with a lowercase l. The display name looks official, but the domain belongs to someone else.
cues: Look-alike sender domain: northbrldge instead of northbridge
The display name imitates IT Services
The link leads to the same fake domain
feedback.safe_action: Do not click. Report the message to IT Services and check your mailbox quota through the official portal.

scenarios.label: legitimate
scenarios.context: It is the second week of the semester.

email.subject: Reminder: add/drop period ends Friday at 23:59
body: Dear students,
This is a reminder that the course add/drop period ends this Friday at 23:59, as published in the academic calendar.
To make changes, sign in to the student portal as you normally do. No reply to this email is needed.
Office of the Registrar

feedback.explanation: This is legitimate. Genuine messages can contain deadlines. This one matches the published academic calendar, makes no threats, comes from the official domain, and tells you to use the portal you already know instead of a link.
cues: The deadline matches the academic calendar
No threats or pressure tactics
It directs you to your usual portal and contains no link
feedback.safe_action: If you need changes, open the student portal yourself before Friday.

scenarios.label: legitimate
scenarios.context: You opened the student portal from your browser bookmark to check your timetable.

web.heading: Student Portal sign in
body: Sign in to see your timetable, grades, and account details.

feedback.explanation: This is legitimate. The registered domain is northbridge.example (portal is simply a subdomain of the official university domain), and you reached the page yourself from a bookmark rather than through a message.
cues: The registered domain is exactly northbridge.example
You navigated there directly from a bookmark
Nothing unusual is requested beyond a normal sign-in
feedback.safe_action: It is safe to sign in. Turn on multi-factor authentication if you have not already.

scenarios.label: phishing
scenarios.context: You applied for a travel scholarship last month.

email.subject: Scholarship payment: verification required
body: Congratulations! Your travel scholarship has been approved.
To release the payment, reply to this email with your student portal username and password so that we can verify your enrollment.
Scholarships Office

feedback.explanation: This is phishing. No genuine office will ever ask for your password. Notice also that replies would go to a free-mail address (freemail.example), not the university, which is a strong sign the sender address was forged.
cues: A direct request for your username and password
The Reply-To address points to an outside free-mail domain
It exploits a believable context: your real application
feedback.safe_action: Never share passwords. Contact the Scholarships Office through the official website and report the email.

scenarios.label: legitimate
scenarios.context: Your project group agreed to share drafts through CloudLocker.

email.subject: Dana Lee shared a folder with you: Group Project Draft
body: Dana Lee (dana.lee@student.northbridge.example) shared a folder with you.
Group Project Draft, 3 files

feedback.explanation: This is legitimate. The link's real destination is on cloudlocker.example, the same domain as the sender, and the share matches what your group agreed. Nothing in the email asks you to re-enter a password.
cues: The link destination matches the service's real domain
An expected share from a known group member
No request for credentials in the message
feedback.safe_action: Open it. If a sign-in page appears, first confirm that the address bar shows cloudlocker.example.

scenarios.label: phishing
scenarios.context: You have not ordered anything online recently.

email.subject: Delivery failed: print the attached label
body: We were unable to deliver your parcel today.
Open the attached shipping label and follow the instructions to reschedule delivery within 48 hours, or the parcel will be returned to the sender.

feedback.explanation: This is phishing. You were not expecting a parcel, the sender's domain is not SwiftParcel's official domain, and the attachment is an .html file, a format often used to open fake sign-in pages or run scripts.
cues: An unexpected delivery notice
A risky attachment type (.html)
A look-alike courier domain and a 48-hour deadline
feedback.safe_action: Do not open the attachment. Track parcels only through the courier's official website or app.

scenarios.label: phishing
scenarios.context: A classmate mentioned that a grades summary was being shared around.

email.subject: A file was shared with you: Final_Grades_Summary.xlsx
body: The Academic Office shared a document with you.
Final_Grades_Summary.xlsx

feedback.explanation: This is phishing. The sender looks like CloudLocker, but the real destination is example-files.test; cloudlocker appears only as a label in front of another domain. Read an address from right to left, starting just before the first single slash.
cues: The real destination differs from the brand's domain
Tempting content (a grades summary) from a vague sender
Sender addresses can be forged
feedback.safe_action: Do not click. Ask the Academic Office through official channels whether they shared anything.

scenarios.label: legitimate
scenarios.context: You use PayWave to pay at the campus cafe.

email.subject: Your monthly statement is ready
body: Your PayWave statement for September is ready.
To view it, open the PayWave app or sign in on the website you normally use.
We will never ask for your password or verification codes by email.

feedback.explanation: This is legitimate. It informs you, contains no link or attachment, and directs you to the app you already use. It also states that PayWave never asks for passwords or codes by email.
cues: Official PayWave domain
No request for passwords or codes
No link: you navigate yourself
feedback.safe_action: View the statement in the app if you wish.

scenarios.label: phishing
scenarios.context: You applied for on-campus housing.

email.subject: URGENT: Your room will be released in 2 hours
body: Your room assignment will be released to the waiting list in 2 HOURS unless you confirm it with a deposit now.
Act immediately:

link.text: Confirm my room and pay the deposit

feedback.explanation: This is phishing. A two-hour deadline and the threat of losing your room are designed to rush your judgment. The domain northbridge-residence.example is not the university domain.
cues: Extreme time pressure
Threat of losing something important
Payment link on an outside domain
feedback.safe_action: Check your housing status through the student portal, or phone the Housing Office using official contact details.

scenarios.label: phishing
scenarios.context: A pop-up said your NorthLearn session had expired, and this page opened.

web.heading: NorthLearn sign in
body: Your session has expired. Sign in again to continue.

feedback.explanation: This is phishing. learn-northbridge.example uses a hyphen to create a completely different domain. The real LMS is learn.northbridge.example, where learn is a subdomain of the official domain.
cues: A hyphenated look-alike domain
An unexpected request to sign in again
The padlock does not prove the site is genuine
feedback.safe_action: Close the page and open NorthLearn from your bookmark.

scenarios.label: legitimate
scenarios.context: You signed up for the Career Center newsletter at orientation.

email.subject: Career fair next Wednesday: employer list inside
body: Hello,
The autumn career fair takes place next Wednesday from 10:00 to 15:00 in the Student Union. Forty employers will attend, including several technology firms.
No registration is needed; just bring your student card.
Career Center

feedback.explanation: This is legitimate. The sender uses the exact official domain, the message matches a newsletter you signed up for, and it asks for nothing sensitive.
cues: Exact official domain after the @ sign
An expected newsletter you subscribed to
No request for information, payment, or sign-in
feedback.safe_action: Attend if you are interested.

scenarios.label: legitimate
scenarios.context: You attended the Photography Club meeting on Tuesday.

email.subject: Minutes from Tuesday's meeting
body: Hi everyone,
Thanks for coming on Tuesday. The minutes are attached, including the dates for next month's photo walk.
Sam, Club Secretary

feedback.explanation: This is legitimate. You attended the meeting, the minutes were expected, the sender uses an official university subdomain, and the file is an ordinary PDF.
cues: An expected document from a meeting you attended
An official university subdomain (groups.northbridge.example)
A common, low-risk file type
feedback.safe_action: It is reasonable to open the minutes.

scenarios.label: phishing
scenarios.context: This email arrives during the first month of the semester.

email.subject: Update your emergency contact details
body: Dear Student,
University policy requires every student to update their emergency contact details this semester.
Complete the secure form using the link below:

feedback.explanation: This is phishing. northbridge-edu.example adds -edu to create a different domain that only resembles the university's. Always compare the full domain after the @ sign.
cues: A look-alike sender domain
Official-sounding policy language
The link goes to the same outside domain
feedback.safe_action: Update contact details only by signing in to the student portal yourself.

scenarios.label: legitimate
scenarios.context: The Health Center publishes its clinic dates on the university website.

email.subject: Reminder: flu vaccination clinic closes Thursday
body: The free flu vaccination clinic runs until Thursday at 16:00 in the Health Center, Room 104.
No appointment is needed. If you miss it, the next clinic will be held in November.
Northbridge Health Center

feedback.explanation: This is legitimate. The deadline is real but low-pressure, there is no threat, and a later alternative is offered. The sender's domain is official, and nothing is requested from you.
cues: A genuine, low-pressure deadline
An alternative is offered instead of a threat
Official domain and no request for information
feedback.safe_action: Attend the clinic if you wish.

scenarios.label: legitimate
scenarios.context: You opened NorthLearn from your bookmark to submit an assignment.

web.heading: NorthLearn sign in
body: Sign in to access your courses and assignments.

feedback.explanation: This is legitimate. learn is a subdomain of the official northbridge.example domain, and you navigated there yourself from a bookmark.
cues: The registered domain is exactly northbridge.example
You arrived from your own bookmark
A normal sign-in page with no unusual requests
feedback.safe_action: It is safe to sign in.

scenarios.label: phishing
scenarios.context: You have a PayWave account.

email.subject: Unusual sign-in: confirm your identity
body: We noticed an unusual sign-in attempt on your account.
We have sent a 6-digit verification code to your phone. Reply to this email with the code within 30 minutes to keep your account active.

feedback.explanation: This is phishing. Verification codes are meant only for you to type into the real app or website. Anyone who asks you to send them a code is trying to take over your account. The Reply-To address is also an outside free-mail domain.
cues: A request to share a one-time code
Reply-To points to a different domain
Time pressure: 30 minutes
feedback.safe_action: Never share codes. Open the PayWave app directly to review your account activity.

scenarios.label: legitimate
scenarios.context: You follow the library's announcements.

email.subject: New research databases are now available
body: Three new research databases are now available to all students, including an IEEE conference archive.
Browse the full list on the library website:

feedback.explanation: This is legitimate. The link's real destination is library.northbridge.example, a subdomain of the official domain, and it matches the sender. No sign-in or personal data is requested.
cues: The link destination matches the official domain
The sender and the link belong to the same organization
No request for credentials
feedback.safe_action: It is safe to follow the link.

scenarios.label: phishing
scenarios.context: You do not have an account with Harbor Bank.

email.subject: Invoice #88213 overdue: see attachment
body: Please find attached the overdue invoice for your recent purchase.
Open the archive and follow the instructions to avoid a late fee.

feedback.explanation: This is phishing. You have no relationship with this bank, the domain is not the bank's official domain, and compressed .zip files are a common way to slip malware past email filters.
cues: An invoice from a company you do not use
A compressed .zip attachment
A look-alike billing domain and a late-fee threat
feedback.safe_action: Do not open the attachment. Delete the email and report it.

scenarios.label: phishing
scenarios.context: You finished last semester with good grades.

email.subject: Congratulations, you made the Dean's List!
body: Congratulations! You have been named to the Dean's List for academic excellence.
Sign in below to download your official certificate and claim your award:

feedback.explanation: This is phishing. Good news is a common lure because it lowers our guard. The sender's domain, northbridge-admin.example, is not the university's domain: every genuine university address ends with exactly northbridge.example.
cues: A look-alike sender domain (northbridge-admin.example)
A flattering reward that lowers suspicion
A sign-in is required to claim the reward
feedback.safe_action: Do not sign in through the link. Check award notices in the student portal and report the email.

scenarios.label: legitimate
scenarios.context: Your instructor said the Unit 3 grades would be posted today.

email.subject: New grade posted: INFO 3310, Unit 3
body: A new grade has been posted for INFO 3310, Unit 3 Assignment.
View the grade and your instructor's comments:

feedback.explanation: This is legitimate. The link's real destination is on learn.northbridge.example, which matches both the sender and the official domain, and the message was expected because your instructor announced it.
cues: The link destination is on the official domain
The sender and the link match
An expected notification you were told about
feedback.safe_action: It is fine to open the link. You can also open NorthLearn from your bookmark.

scenarios.label: phishing
scenarios.context: You use CampusConnect, the student social app.

email.subject: Your account will be deleted in 24 hours
body: We received reports that your account violated our community policy.
Your account and all of your photos will be permanently deleted in 24 hours unless you appeal now.

feedback.explanation: This is phishing. A threat of permanent deletion within 24 hours is designed to make you panic and act before you think. The domain campusconnect-support.example is not CampusConnect's real domain (campusconnect.example).
cues: A threat of permanent loss
A short, artificial deadline
A look-alike support domain
feedback.safe_action: Open the CampusConnect app directly to check for any real notices, and report the email.

scenarios.label: legitimate
scenarios.context: Yesterday, you requested an enrollment verification letter through the student portal.

email.subject: Your requested enrollment verification letter
body: Dear student,
As requested through the student portal on Monday, your enrollment verification letter is attached.
Office of the Registrar

feedback.explanation: This is legitimate. You requested this document yourself, the sender uses the official domain, and a PDF letter is exactly what you asked for.
cues: You requested this attachment
Official Registrar address
An ordinary PDF document
feedback.safe_action: It is reasonable to open the letter.

scenarios.label: phishing
scenarios.context: In the library, you joined a Wi-Fi network called Northbridge-Free-WiFi. This page appeared.

web.heading: Wi-Fi access
body: To keep browsing, re-enter your student portal username and password.

feedback.explanation: This is phishing. The page asks for your university password on an unencrypted (http) page hosted on wifi-northbridge.test, which is not the university domain. Fake hotspots often imitate campus networks to collect passwords.
cues: A request for your portal password
No HTTPS: the connection is not encrypted
A domain unrelated to northbridge.example
feedback.safe_action: Disconnect, and join only the official campus network listed on the IT Services website.

scenarios.label: legitimate
scenarios.context: You typed portal.northbridge.example into the address bar yourself to check your financial aid.

web.heading: Financial aid summary
body: Academic year 2026 to 2027
Status: award letter available
Next disbursement: 15 October

feedback.explanation: This is legitimate. You typed the address yourself, the registered domain is northbridge.example, and the page shows information rather than asking for secrets.
cues: You navigated directly by typing the address
The registered domain is exactly northbridge.example
No request for passwords or codes
feedback.safe_action: It is safe to use this page.
